context: The n elements are distinct. The gray root at the top represents the state before any choice. Each level in a dashed box below it fills the next position. The right-hand brace labeled “n levels” spans only the choice levels below the root, excluding the root itself.
description: The left column gives the number of branches from each node at the preceding level. The right column gives the total nodes on the current level. Ellipses represent intermediate levels. Small n requires only the choice levels that actually occur, so the last row may coincide with an earlier row.

frames.explanation: The formula at the bottom, n × (n−1) × … × 1 = n!, counts the green leaves on the bottom level. Each leaf represents a complete permutation and contributes one base-case count to the value returned by factorial_recur. The value n! counts leaves only. Even including the root and all intermediate levels, the tree has fewer than 3 times n! nodes. Each call contains a loop, but each loop iteration creates exactly one edge to a child call. The tree has one fewer edge than nodes, so including the loop work still gives O(n!). This counts constant work per edge and excludes the extra cost of copying complete permutations.
frames.title: Choosing a permutation one position at a time gives factorial growth

summary: Each time we fill another position in a permutation, one fewer element remains available. Multiplying the numbers of choices gives the total number of permutations.
